title: Check commands ignore a leaked GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE too
brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24. Read src/util.ts: `GIT_ENV_LEAKS` and `git()` already drop GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE from the env; `shell()` builds `const env = { ...process.env, ...opts.env }`. Check commands and bench go through shell(), so a leak still breaks them. Adapters with isolateGit pass their own GIT_DIR in opts.env and that must keep working.
1. In shell(): start from a copy of process.env without the GIT_ENV_LEAKS keys (same case-insensitive filter as git()), then spread opts.env on top. Keep the CLAUDECODE delete.
2. In test/pick.ts, after the existing GIT_DIR test (before `pick PASS`): with process.env.GIT_DIR = "/nonexistent", `await shell("git rev-parse --git-dir", { cwd: <a temp git repo>, timeoutMs: 30_000 })` has code 0; and `await shell("echo $GIT_DIR", { cwd, timeoutMs: 30_000, env: { GIT_DIR: "/x" } })` prints /x. Restore the env afterwards. Import shell from ../src/util.ts.
Change nothing else.

title: RELATED FILES: one line per relation, no imports/imports_from pairs
brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24. Read fileNeighbours in src/graph.ts and test/graph.ts. Graphify emits both `imports` and `imports_from` for the same import, so each line shows up twice ("src/cli.ts imports src/graph.ts" and "src/cli.ts imports_from src/graph.ts").
1. In fileNeighbours, normalise the relation by removing a trailing `_from` (imports_from -> imports) before building the line, so the existing Set deduplicates it.
2. In test/graph.ts add a case: a graph where x.ts has both an `imports` and an `imports_from` link to a.ts gives exactly one line "x.ts imports a.ts" for files ["a.ts"]. Keep the existing assertions passing.
Change nothing else.

title: Lessons: reuse followUps(), follow-ups only from the newest run
brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24. Read src/lessons.ts (pastLessons, a private followUps copy) and `export function followUps(report: string): string[]` in src/nodes/flow.ts (parses a `## Follow-ups` section, handles wrapped bullets and drops 'None.').
Problem from a real run: follow-ups of older runs that were since fixed keep coming back as lessons.
1. Delete the private followUps in src/lessons.ts and import followUps from "./nodes/flow.ts".
2. Take follow-up lines only from the newest selected run (index 0 after sorting); failed/skipped/retried task lines still come from all selected runs. Keep the order: for each run, task lines, then (newest run only) follow-up lines.
3. Update test/lessons.ts: follow-ups of an older run are no longer included; the newest run's still are. Keep the other assertions.
Change nothing else.
